citations.long: Failure to reject any lot of components that did not meet the appropriate written specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.

citations.short: Written records kept in individual logs
citations.long: Written records of major equipment cleaning, maintenance, and use are not included in individual equipment logs.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.

Laboratory records do not include the initials or signature of a second person showing that the original records have been reviewed for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

Reports of analysis from component suppliers are accepted in lieu of testing each component for conformity with all appropriate written specifications, without establishing the reliability of the supplier's analyses through appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.

There are no written procedures for production and process controls designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess.
Deviations from written production and process control procedures are not recorded and justified.
